messages:
diane-customer: Hey team — we've got a customer reporting partial SSE output followed by a duplicate charge when their client reconnects. They see the text cut off, then reconnect and receive the rest *and* a second full generation. Billing doubled. Repro steps attached.
alice-cs: Thanks for the heads-up. Can you paste the minimal repro and the client behavior? Is their client using exponential backoff + restart or attempting a resume token? :thinking_face:
repro-bot: Repro gist: https://internal.gists/repro/abcd1234 — client logs show SSE disconnect 1s after stream start, then immediate reconnect with previous session-id header and no idempotency key.
ben-eng: If they're re-opening a fresh request but keep the same session-id, server treats it as a new generation. That will bill again. Do we have a resume-token mechanism in the SDK for partial outputs? They might be trying to "hydrate" the missing chunk by issuing the full prompt again.
charlie-ml: Correct — our resume semantics are explicit: resume_token lets you continue a partially emitted response without re-executing model generation; without it, a retry is a full new request. Also note we only dedupe on an idempotency-key within a short window (60s) and when the request signature matches.
alice-cs: Diane — pls confirm whether the client attempted to replay with the same prompt body or used a smaller tail-chunk request. Also include network trace if possible.
diane-customer: They re-sent the original POST body to /v1/streams with header `Session-Id: xyz-9` after the disconnect. No Idempotency-Key header. They didn't see a resume token in the first stream because it cut before the server emitted resume metadata.
ben-eng: That explains it. When the stream cuts before resume metadata, client can't resume. Two paths:
1) Client uses an idempotency-key on the *request* so server can dedupe duplicate full requests (good for short-term retries).
2) Better: implement resume_token emission early in stream initialization so clients can safely reconnect and resume instead of retrying a full generation.
charlie-ml: For short-term mitigation recommend attaching an `Idempotency-Key` (uuid) to every stream request. Our backend will attempt dedupe for identical bodies + idempotency key within 120s. Example header: `Idempotency-Key: 8a6f...`.
alice-cs: Also advise backoff: on disconnect do exponential backoff and, on first reconnect, request `?mode=resume` with `Resume-Token: <token>` if available; otherwise, use same idempotency-key to avoid a second charge.
diane-customer: Customer says they can't change client quickly. Any server-side workaround we can apply per-customer? They hit billing for 4 duplicates.
ben-eng: We can retroactively detect near-identical requests from same session-id in a short window and issue a credit manually, but that's manual ops. For auto behavior we'd need to relax dedupe window which has risk.
charlie-ml: I can add a short-term heuristic: if we see request B within 10s of disconnect from same session-id and same prompt fingerprint, mark as probable duplicate and hold billing until final confirmation. Needs ops + billing sign-off.
alice-cs: For now, Diane — please offer customer this checklist:
- Explain cause: reconnect without resume_token -> full re-gen.
- Workaround: add Idempotency-Key header on first try (SDK patch example below).
- Backoff: wait 200-500ms jittered, then 2x, etc. Avoid immediate replays.
- Long term: update client to honor resume_token and prefer resume mode.
alice-cs: SDK pseudocode to attach idempotency key:
```
const id = uuidv4();
fetch('/v1/streams', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
    'Idempotency-Key': id
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
```
ben-eng: And if you want a server-side repro: run this sequence (shell):
```
# 1) start stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
# kill after 1s
# 2) immediate replay without idempotency key
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
```
You will see two charged generations.
diane-customer: Customer accepted the temporary credit. They're going to patch their client next week to add idempotency keys. Can we log this case so Product considers emitting resume metadata earlier (first bytes)?
charlie-ml: Filed an internal feature request: EMIT-RESUME-EARLY-2165. Suggestion: include a small resume token envelope as part of initial handshake frame so clients can resume even if first content chunk drops.
alice-cs: Great. I'll send the customer-facing note and the mitigation steps. Closing the escalation after credit and SDK guidance shared. :white_check_mark:
